documents_checked.document_title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Policy
documents_checked.text:
Principle 6: Transparency, Explainability and Contestability
Develop, deploy and use AI systems in a way that maximises transparency,
explainability and contestability. Allow stakeholders to know when AI has
been used and contest decisions made using AI.
Principle 7: Accountability
Implement human oversight, review and the ability to intervene for all AI-
based functions and decisions. Identify the individual accountable for any
decision made using AI. Maintain records on the use of AI to comply with
recordkeeping obligations.

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: An accountable human and meaningful review or effective correction of AI evaluations determining binding academic marks.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: N002 PC2 s.2.4 prohibits unverified AI grading by restricting AI grading/feedback to approved staff pilots with mandatory staff output verification and human marking on appeal, reinforced by N002 s.2.8 and N001 Principles 6-7.
case_summary.case_note: Curtin's N002 PC2 s.2.4 restricts GenAI grading or feedback to staff pilots approved by the Dean (Learning and Teaching), Privacy Officer, and CIO/CISO, requiring staff verification of all outputs, advance student declaration, and human marking on appeal. Combined with fair group mark allocation (N002 s.2.8) and AI accountability and contestability (N001), unreviewed AI evaluations cannot determine binding marks (D5=3, Critical gap=No). Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15.
